match.reason: No bank point defines standard deviation as a measure of spread for Stage 5 students; the closest cards assume normal distributions, z-scores or the empirical rule, which are a different and deeper idea.

draft.title: Standard deviation
card: Standard deviation measures how far values typically are from the mean. It is a measure of spread, written \(\sigma\) for a whole population.
A small standard deviation means the values are clustered close to the mean. A large one means they are spread out.
Use the statistics mode of a calculator. Enter the data, then read the value labelled \(\sigma\). Do not work it out by hand.
Example: 5, 5, 5, 5 and 1, 5, 5, 9 both have mean 5. The first has standard deviation 0. The second has a larger one, because its values lie further from 5.
draft.remember: Standard deviation is the typical distance from the mean: small means clustered, large means spread out.

a.q: A dataset has a very small standard deviation. What does this tell you about the values?
opts: They are clustered close to the mean
They are spread far from the mean
They are all smaller than the mean
They are all equal to the median
a.why: Standard deviation is the typical distance from the mean, so a small value means the data is close to the mean. It does not say the values are below the mean or equal to the median.
a.clue: Small spread means the values stay near the mean.

b.q: Two bakeries in Orange weigh their loaves. Both have a mean of 800 g. Bakery P has a standard deviation of 4 g and Bakery Q has 15 g. Which bakery has more consistent loaf weights?
opts: Bakery P, because its weights are closer to the mean
Bakery Q, because its weights are closer to the mean
Bakery P, because its standard deviation is larger
Neither, because the means are the same
b.why: The smaller standard deviation of 4 g means P's weights cluster closer to 800 g, so P is more consistent. Equal means do not make equal spread, because standard deviation measures spread.
b.clue: Compare the standard deviations, not the means.

a.best: They are clustered close to the mean

b.best: Bakery P, because its weights are closer to the mean

problems.detail: The clue 'Small spread means the values stay near the mean' restates the right option almost word for word, so a student can pick it without knowing what standard deviation measures.

check.summary: The card, the remember line, both answers and the explanations are correct. The only problem is that question a's clue gives the answer away by restating the right option.
